ai.title: Fix system message serialization in checkNewFilesNecessary
ai.summary: checkNewFilesNecessary now correctly serializes system messages that are passed as arrays of objects instead of strings. Previously, array inputs were coerced into '[object Object]' within the prompt construction. The fix maps array elements to their text properties and joins them with newlines before interpolation. Affects backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts.

eli5.text: You may have seen the words [object Object] appear in a system message where text should have been. The assistant now reads each message in a list and pulls out its text before putting it into the prompt. The garbled placeholder is gone, and the message reads as the actual words instead.

ai.title: endturn description requires turn end before questions
ai.summary: The `end_turn` tool description in `backend/src/tools.ts` now explicitly instructs the agent to end its turn before asking the user any questions. This change clarifies that failing to call `end_turn` prevents the user from responding. The mechanism ensures the conversation loop remains active for user input.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes answering you and has a question to ask, it now has to signal the end of its turn before posing that question; otherwise the chat interface stays open and waiting for a reply that can never arrive, so your response gets skipped. This keeps the back-and-forth loop active so you can always jump back in with an answer or next instruction. The updated wording is live today in the assistant's built-in tool reference.

ai.title: Web landing updates: install dialog, hero button, editor logos, README
ai.summary: Landing hero button text changed from "Try Free" to "Get Started" with visual refinements. Install dialog rewritten as step-by-step guide with editor launch buttons (VS Code, Cursor, IntelliJ, PyCharm) and copy-to-clipboard commands. Competitor logos moved from web/public/competitors/ to web/public/logos/ with new IDE icons added. README simplified to single `bun install && bun run build` command.

eli5.text: When you visit the landing page and click the big button in the hero section, it now says 'Get Started' instead of 'Try Free'. Clicking that button opens a new step-by-step installation guide that walks you through each editor (VS Code, Cursor, IntelliJ, PyCharm) and lets you copy the terminal command with one click. The competitor logos like Cursor and Claude Code were moved into a shared 'logos' folder and new IDE icons were added, so the guide shows recognizable pictures next to each option. If you're building the project from source, the README's setup instructions were simplified to a single command.

ai.title: Strikethrough on gitignored files in tool renderers
ai.summary: tool-renderers.ts applies strikethrough and '(blocked)' to gitignored files in tool call displays. isFileIgnored from common/project-file-tree checks paths against project root. Affects file listing and path parameter rendering. No user action required.

eli5.text: When the assistant shows you a list of files it is working with, any file that is on the project's ignore list now appears crossed out and labeled with '(blocked)', so you can tell at a glance which files were intentionally left out. This visual cue only applies to the file-listing and path displays inside the assistant's tool outputs, and it took effect with the update dated 2025-05-03; if you notice a file is crossed out, it simply means the project's settings tell the assistant not to include that file.

ai.title: fix scripts importing bigquery
ai.summary: Added `setupBigQuery` call in `scripts/ft-file-selection/print-recent-traces.ts` and declared `@codebuff/bigquery` dependency in `scripts/package.json`. Fixes runtime errors when scripts execute without BigQuery client initialization. Scope limited to internal tooling scripts.

eli5.text: Internal scripts that read recent activity from the data warehouse now set up their connection properly before fetching data, so they no longer crash mid-run. The change affects only internal tooling scripts. You wouldn't see anything as an end user, it just prevents errors from appearing in the backend logs that keep the site running.

ai.title: DEBUG flag gates truncateFileTreeBasedOnTokenBudget logs
ai.summary: Added const DEBUG = false in backend/src/system-prompt/truncate-file-tree.ts to conditionally execute logger.debug calls within truncateFileTreeBasedOnTokenBudget. This silences verbose token budget and duration metrics for unimportant-files, tokens, and depth-based truncation levels by default. The change is isolated to the file tree truncation subsystem. Existing logger.warn calls remain unaffected.

eli5.text: You won't see any difference in how the assistant writes code or answers questions. Behind the scenes, the team turned off a set of detailed logs that were recording how long it took to trim the list of files down to fit within a size limit. Those logs were only visible to the engineers running the software, so turning them off does not change anything you experience.

ai.title: Add start-max npm script
ai.summary: Adds `start-max` script to `npm-app/package.json` and root `package.json`. Passes `--max` flag to `ts-node` execution. Enables local dev runs with max settings.

eli5.text: A new way to run the application locally has been added, letting developers start it with all the maximum settings already enabled instead of the default configuration. This adds a new option to the project's run commands that was previously only available by passing special flags manually. Developers who want to test or use the full-powered version of the application can now start it with a single command instead of typing extra options each time. The feature is in place and ready to use today.

ai.title: Refine prompt guidance and readfiles tool description
ai.summary: Updated system prompts in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to remove XML-style tags from tool invocation instructions and streamline plan handling logic. The `read_files` tool description in `backend/src/tools.ts` no longer mandates reading files before writing. These changes aim to reduce redundant file reads and clarify experimental thinking modes.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions were cleaned up to make its reasoning steps clearer and less wordy. Specifically, when the assistant is thinking through a complex problem, it no longer needs to surround its internal reasoning with XML-style tags, and the guidance telling it to read files before editing them was removed. This means the assistant will spend less of your time reading the same files over and over before making changes. These adjustments are part of an internal update and are live today.

ai.title: Fix flaky new lines after tool call header
ai.summary: Updated `defaultToolCallRenderer` in `npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts` to track tool start state via a new `toolStart` variable. This logic strips leading newlines from parameter chunks immediately following a tool header, resolving flaky spacing issues in console output. Scope limited to internal rendering logic within the npm-app package. The fix relies on a simple state flag reset on `onToolStart` and consumed on `onParamChunk`.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts using a tool, it will no longer add an extra blank line before showing the tool's parameter content in the console, fixing inconsistent spacing. The rendering logic now skips any leading newline from the first chunk of parameter data that appears right after a tool call header, and this state resets each time a new tool call begins. This behind-the-scenes adjustment affects only how output is displayed internally and is live today.

ai.title: CI: add GITHUBTOKEN to allow tree-sitter library download
ai.summary: CI workflow updated to include GITHUB_TOKEN in environment variables. This token allows the tree-sitter library to be downloaded successfully during the build process. Changes affect .github/workflows/ci.yml.

eli5.text: The continuous integration (CI) pipeline was updated to automatically pass a GitHub authentication token when fetching the tree-sitter library during builds. This ensures the library can be downloaded without manual setup, so automated checks and deployments that rely on it will work correctly. You wouldn't notice anything directly; this is a behind-the-scenes fix to keep the build process reliable. This change is live as of the update.

ai.title: Implement prompt history in CLI
ai.summary: Added prompt history functionality to the CLI. New methods _loadHistory and _appendToHistory manage a JSON file at CONFIG_DIR/prompt_history.json, deduplicating and reversing entries for readline integration. Scope limited to npm-app/src/cli.ts. History persists across sessions, filtering empty/duplicate lines.

eli5.text: When you type commands into the assistant's command-line interface, your recent prompts are now saved to a private file on your computer and made available the next time you open the terminal. If you look at the interface, pressing the up and down arrow keys will cycle through your earlier prompts, skipping any blank or repeated lines. The saved history is shared across every time you launch the tool, so your past questions stay ready to reuse without retyping them.

ai.title: Reset consecutiveAssistantMessages counter after duration log
ai.summary: Added `agentState.consecutiveAssistantMessages = 0` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` immediately after duration calculation. This clears the counter tracking repeated assistant messages to prevent premature force-stop loops. Scope limited to backend state management. Counter reset occurs before terminal command logging.

eli5.text: The system keeps a running tally of how many times the assistant has responded in a row so it can catch endless loops where the assistant keeps repeating itself instead of stopping. After that counter was being used, this change immediately resets it to zero at the same moment the system records how long the action took, preventing the safety cutoff from triggering too soon on the next round. The timing matters because the reset happens before the system logs any follow-up commands, so each new step starts from a clean count. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment that is live today, and most people running or interacting with the backend won't notice it directly since it only prevents an occasional premature shutdown.

ai.title: Fix triple newlines
ai.summary: The `display.ts` module replaced its previous regex-based newline squashing with a terminal-kit `ScreenBuffer` approach. The new implementation strips ANSI escape codes to accurately identify blank lines, capping consecutive empty lines at two. This change ensures consistent output formatting regardless of color codes. Dependencies in `package.json` were updated to include `@types/terminal-kit`.

eli5.text: The text you see on your screen no longer gets extra blank lines squeezed in by accident. Previously, the program looked for three straight line breaks to clean up, but it missed cases where color codes sat between the breaks, leaving awkward gaps. Now it strips out the color-formatting codes first, then counts the real blank lines and caps them at two. If you use the app in a terminal, spaced-out output will look consistently tidy instead of sometimes showing triple gaps.

ai.title: Fix newline squashing across chunk boundaries in display.ts
ai.summary: Newline squashing logic in `npm-app/src/display.ts` now tracks trailing blank state across write chunks. Previously, `squashVisibleNewlines` processed each chunk independently, causing blank line collapse errors when chunks split mid-stream. The new `squashVisibleNewlinesFromBuffer` function combines previous buffer state with incoming chunks, ensuring consistent blank line limits (max 2) across boundaries. Scope limited to internal terminal display buffering; no API or model changes.

eli5.text: When the assistant streams text to your terminal, that text is sent in small pieces rather than one big block. Previously a piece could land in the middle of a blank line, so the next piece would collapse two or more blank lines into one instead of keeping them as intended. The program now remembers how blank lines were left off at the end of each piece, so it keeps the right number of blank lines and you see the spacing it meant to show.

ai.title: Revert display newline squashing logic
ai.summary: Reverts the complex `terminal-kit` ScreenBuffer-based newline squashing in `npm-app/src/display.ts` back to a simple string replacement mechanism. The previous implementation caused rendering artifacts with ANSI escape codes and failed to correctly handle split chunks across stdout writes. This change removes the `@types/terminal-kit` dependency from `npm-app/package.json` and restores the lightweight `previous` buffer tracking.

eli5.text: When the app shows too many blank lines in a row in the terminal, it removes the extras to keep the output tidy. This update reverts a recent, complicated fix back to the original, simpler method for doing that job. You won't notice a difference unless you were running the tool in a terminal and seeing glitches where colored or formatted text was getting cut up or misaligned across lines. The developers determined the newer approach was causing more problems than it solved, so they undid it.
